analysis:
Examined CBv2OwnedRequestState.swift (head lines 1-946) and CBv2StageKVHost.swift. The PR adds two submit paths (asyncEval variants) and a counter. Both new paths are `submit` (lines 317-348) and `submitBatch` (862-920); the host gains a diagnostic counter `submittedDeviceFrontierReads` (patch at line ~355). Reviewed the changes against the TB-007 inference-engine boundary and A-001 (plaintext prompts in process memory), plus T-041, the only supplied definition.

Behavior of the new paths: both refuse packed storage; `submit` additionally requires a paged host. Both keep requireOpen, capacity and reservation checks, and the host-frontier and row-binding validation. Per-row validation and the recurrent generation check run before commit, and any error sets isFailed (lines 344-347, 916-919). Failure marks every row failed, so partially advanced KV is never reused. `submit` skips `checkStepWrites`, which only matters for packed storage, and packed storage is refused. The deferred device-side evaluation of output values and native errors relies on the caller's MLX.withError, which is outside the supplied evidence. `submitBatch` does not call host.finishStep(); whether the caller does so is not visible here. The contiguous host path in submitBatch reads frontiers from the device, which waits on the frame; it is only less overlapped, not weaker.

No prefix-cache, SSD, encryption, key, attestation, or network surface is touched, so T-041 is not affected: no new at-rest artifacts, and no change to cache scoping or TTL. I found no new data exposure, authorization change, or isolation regression. Residual questions for integration: callers (TensorParallelOneTokenLoop, QwenTensorParallelBatchDriver) were not supplied, so I could not verify that they read or evaluate the output under MLX.withError before releasing tokens, that they call finishStep, or that they retire failed states. These are correctness and availability questions, not demonstrated security regressions.
